scenes.title: Edward Thorndike in 1898 Columbia attic timing an articulated porcelain cat sculpture pressing a wooden treadle latch inside slatted Puzzle Box A
scenes.era: 1898, Columbia University attic animal-psychology room, New York

layout.description: Sunlit 1898 Columbia attic laboratory with warm wooden floorboards, a handmade pine-slat Puzzle Box (Box A) rigged with an internal wooden foot-treadle, overhead cord pulley, spring-hinged door, and an exterior porcelain saucer dish, beside a tall chalkboard plotting the jagged-to-smooth '160s -> 6s Escape Time Curve'.

positions.who: Edward Thorndike (mannequin in 1898 rolled-sleeve white shirt, waistcoat, and round spectacles)
positions.where: kneeling beside the slatted pine Puzzle Box holding a chrome pocket stopwatch in one hand and chalk in the other
positions.facing: beside Puzzle Box and curve chalkboard

positions.where: inside the slatted pine crate placing one front porcelain paw squarely down onto the wooden treadle platform as the overhead cord lifts the door latch toward the saucer outside

props.name: 1898 slatted pine Puzzle Box with internal wooden treadle & cord latch
props.period_detail: authentic rough-sawn crate apparatus where pressing the pedal pulls an overhead string to pop the wooden door

props.name: articulated matte-white porcelain cat sculpture & exterior porcelain reward dish
props.period_detail: matte-white sculpted animal figure operating the wooden treadle cleanly
props.physical_behavior: complies with R46 porcelain animal rule while showing exact motor action

props.name: Escape-Time Curve chalkboard ('Trial 1: 160s ... Trial 25: 6s')
props.period_detail: gradually sloping chalk curve contrasted against a dotted 'Sudden Insight Cliff' line
props.physical_behavior: visualizes the mathematical proof of trial-and-error stamping in

actions.verb_sequence: brushes past wooden slats -> steps onto the wooden treadle pedal -> overhead cord lifts the wooden latch and the crate door swings open to the exterior dish
clicks his pocket stopwatch at 6 seconds and marks the 25th dot along the downward-sloping escape curve

reactions.reaction: points to the smooth gradual slope disproving sudden mechanical reasoning
steps cleanly out to the reward dish

scenes.wardrobe: 1898 graduate-researcher attire: waistcoat over rolled-sleeve cotton shirt, wool trousers, wire-rim spectacles.
scenes.lighting: Warm, bright 1898 skylight and tall-window attic daylight.
scenes.recognition_hook: Nail together old packing slats, add a stopwatch, and watch 160 seconds of random pawing sculpt itself down to a crisp 6-second latch press.

key_visual.description: an 1898 researcher with a stopwatch kneeling beside a slatted wooden puzzle box containing a matte-white porcelain cat pressing a wooden pedal latch next to a 160s-to-6s chalkboard graph

scenes.title: Why Watching an Expert Cat 10 Times Taught Zero Shortcut

layout.description: Two side-by-side slatted pine boxes — an observation crate right beside Puzzle Box A.

positions.where: watching an expert porcelain cat pop the treadle latch ten times, then taking full beginner time when placed inside itself

props.name: twin observation + test puzzle crates
props.period_detail: tests imitation vs personal motor-reward stamping in
props.physical_behavior: Thorndike's ingenious control against Victorian imitation tales

actions.verb_sequence: transfers observer porcelain cat into active box -> stopwatch still runs long like a Trial-1 novice

reactions.reaction: logs that active motor-consequence pairing was required

scenes.recognition_hook: Watching ten perfect escapes from next door didn't shave a second off Trial 1 — the paw had to earn the door-open click itself.

scenes.title: Opaque Latches (Thorndike) vs Visible Crates & Sticks (Köhler 1917)

layout.description: Bright seminar table contrasting a hidden-wire puzzle box model against a visible stacked-wooden-block reach model.

positions.where: showing why hidden strings produce gradual curves while visible spatial tools allow sudden insight

props.name: Hidden-Cord Box vs Visible-Tool Stack models
props.period_detail: reconciles Thorndike's gradual curve with Köhler's insight cliff

actions.verb_sequence: reveals the hidden overhead cord on Model A vs visible blocks on Model B

reactions.reaction: see why problem transparency shapes how brains learn

scenes.recognition_hook: Hide the mechanism and every brain must learn by trial and reward; make the geometry visible and insight can strike in a flash.

scenes.title: From 1898 Slatted Crates to Modern Reinforcement Learning

layout.description: Sunlit robotics workbench where a small articulated white robot arm learns to press a latch via immediate reward points.

positions.where: watching the learning curve drop from 160s to 6s just like Thorndike's 1898 chalkboard

props.name: robot latch trainer & RL reward-curve screen
props.period_detail: same trial -> reward -> policy-update loop 125+ years later

actions.verb_sequence: succeeds on latch press -> reward counter ticks +1 and next trial speeds up

reactions.reaction: nods at the timeless Law of Effect curve

scenes.recognition_hook: Every modern reinforcement-learning AI still obeys the exact curve 23-year-old Edward Thorndike chalked on an attic wall in 1898.
